evidence.curator_note: First transformation of Equation 8.66, labelled '(alpha)' over a plain straight reaction arrow. GENERIC SCHEME: the page draws an alicyclic alcohol whose ring is closed by a curl (a polymethylene bridge of unspecified length); the surrounding text (page 187) covers cycloalkyl-OH compounds of five- to at least eight-membered rings. INSTANTIATION: cyclohexanol (6-ring, M+. m/z 100.088), chosen to match the six-membered middle column of Equation 8.65 on the facing page; every m/z in this record derives from that curator-chosen instantiation and is NOT printed by the book. Atom maps: 1 = O, 2 = the carbinol carbon C1, 3 = the ring carbon C2 that carries the transferred H (map 8), 4-6 = the bridge carbons C3-C5, 7 = the ring CH2 (C6) whose bond to C1 is cleaved. The molecular ion is n-ionized at oxygen ('+.' drawn over the HO group), and alpha-cleavage of the C1-C6 ring bond forms the O=C1 head, leaving the CH2 radical terminus. Book draws 0 arcs for this step; NO move is drawn - moves <1,2,3> (the O odd electron into the forming O=C1 pi bond, one C1-C6 sigma electron into that same pi bond, and the implicit homolysis hook putting the other C1-C6 electron on C6) are all curator-supplied and required for electron balance (not drawn on the page). RESONANCE / DRAWN-STRUCTURE DISCLOSURE: the page draws this intermediate in the CARBENIUM resonance form - a plain HO- single bond with '+' written under the carbinol carbon and '.' on the CH2 - and draws the C1...C6 bond as a DOTTED, incompletely dissociated bond (that is the whole point of the equation: 'the C-C bond alpha to the heteroatom does not fully dissociate before the H transfer; the incipient -CH2. radical can remain weakly bound to the charged heteroatom functional group'). Per convention (C) one localized form is encoded consistently, and the oxocarbenium partner HO+=CH- is used here so the arrows balance; the residual weak C1...C6 interaction the book dots in is NOT encoded as a bond. The ring-opened species is still a single connected molecule (the chain C1-C2-C3-C4-C5-C6 survives), so it is a legitimate mapped_smiles species.

Second transformation of Equation 8.66, labelled 'rH': the H on the ring carbon adjacent to the carbinol carbon (map 8 on atom 3) is transferred to the CH2 radical terminus (atom 7, which becomes CH3), the C1=C2 double bond forms, and the charge/odd electron end up on oxygen - the page draws the product as HO(+.)-CH=CH-...-CH3, an acyclic enol radical cation that is an ISOMER of the molecular ion (no mass is lost in Equation 8.66). Book draws 1 arc for this step: a single fishhook running from the transferred H down onto the .CH2 terminus; that arc is move <2> (one electron of the C2-H bond travelling with the H into the new C6-H bond). Moves <1,3,4,5> are implicit and required for electron balance (not drawn on the page): <1> the C6 odd electron into the new C6-H bond, <3> the other C2-H electron into the forming C1=C2 pi bond, <4> one electron of the O=C1 pi bond into that same C1=C2 bond, and <5> the other O=C1 pi electron back onto oxygen, regenerating the O(+.) the book draws on the product. The 1,5-H transfer from C3 to C7 (donor and acceptor are four bonds apart along C3-C4-C5-C6-C7; an earlier version of this note said '1,4-H transfer from C2 to C6', which mis-stated both the shift order and the atom maps - the encoded moves are bond[3,8]->bond[7,8]) is geometrically possible only because of the residual weak C1...C6 bonding the book dots into the intermediate; that non-covalent contact is disclosed here and not encoded.

rule_index.json 'by_equation' has NO entry for 8.66 (its chapter-8 keys stop at 8.14), so no MOD rule variable is cross-linked. Candidates checked and REJECTED: (i) IMS_4_9 'radical induced (alpha-)clevage for a saturated site', DFS [C]1[C]2[C]3([C]4)[_A+.]5>>[C.]1.[C]2[C]3([C]4){=}[_A+.]5 - it cleaves C1-C2, a bond NOT incident to C3, the atom that forms the new pi bond to the heteroatom, so its geometry is not the alpha-cleavage of this scheme; it also keeps [_A+.] on the product heteroatom while creating [C.]1, i.e. one unpaired electron becomes two, which fails the L->R spin conservation the rules/__init__.py guardrail enforces, so the rule is auto-dropped from the fragmentation list. (ii) IMS_4_13_1 is correctly encoded (the cleaved C1-C5 bond IS incident to C5, the atom that forms C5=O8) but is hard-wired to a dialkyl ETHER skeleton C-C-O(+.)-C-C, so its pattern cannot match a secondary alcohol HO(H)-C. (iii) hTransition_saturated_1 (DFS [H]1[C]2[C]3[C]4[C]5[_A+.]6) delivers the H onto the HETEROATOM, so it does not describe this step. hTransition_saturated_2 (DFS [H]1[C]2[C]3([_A+]4)[C]5[C.]6 >> [C.]2[C]3([_A+]4)[C]5[C]6([H]1)) DOES move the H onto a carbon radical terminus - the same kind of step as this one (an earlier version of this note claimed the opposite; that was wrong, verified against IMS_bookCover.py). It is nevertheless REJECTED here on geometry: the rule is a 1,4-shift whose onium [_A+]4 sits on the carbon BETWEEN donor and acceptor (chain C2-C3-C5-C6), whereas Eq 8.66 is a 1,5-shift (donor C3, acceptor C7, four bonds apart) whose oxocarbenium O1=C2 sits on the far side of the donor, outside the donor->acceptor chain. Chain length and charge-site placement both differ, so the rule cannot match this substrate.

NO m/z and NO intensity are printed anywhere on Equation 8.66 - the scheme is generic (curl = unspecified polymethylene bridge) and its product is an isomerization product, not a fragment. observed_mz 100.0883 is the monoisotopic m/z of C6H12O+. computed by the curator from the chosen cyclohexanol instantiation (it is identical to the molecular-ion m/z, since no neutral is lost); status is 'inferred' and the species is detected=false. The book does not present this ion as an independently observed peak.
